findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion asserting the state AFTER a flag-ON->OFF rollback: a plain-wire reconcile pass over bodies already rendered as wiki/ADF under cutover performs no body update and raises no spurious conflict (attach a DATA LOSS RISK note for the DC lossy one-way path, since the rendered wiki cannot be inverted to the pre-cutover source).
evidence: Plan: 'DC is a one-way Markdown->wiki renderer' and 'Jira wiki markup is lossy for punctuation-dense prose, so the DC path must not rely on codec fixed points'
The rollback AC asserts the wire path reverts (plain/identity) but names no assertion on already-rendered remote bodies after the flag is turned off
Sibling AC 'test_cutover_does_not_mass_rewrite_already_synced_bodies' covers the flag-ON convergence case, not the flag-ON->OFF transition over already-rendered bodies
findings.finding: The cutover is a one-way, lossy transformation of live Jira bodies (DC Markdown->wiki has no inverse), yet the rollback AC only asserts the outbound WIRE reverts to plain/identity; the plan does not assert the state after rollback for bodies already pushed as rendered wiki/ADF — specifically that a subsequent flag-OFF (plain-wire) pass reads those already-rendered remote bodies back cleanly and does not mass-rewrite or re-emit them.
findings.location: disparaged-parodistic-shrew AC 'Flag-gated, defaults OFF ... reverting to the plain/identity wire when off (test_cutover_rollback_restores_plain)'; Design 'Missing pandoc, timeout, or pathological input falls back without data loss'
scenarios: An operator enables rich_text_cutover=dc, several descriptions/comments are rewritten to rendered wiki, then the flag is turned OFF; the next plain-wire reconcile pass compares raw Markdown local against the rendered-wiki remote/baseline and either mass re-emits every body or flags spurious conflicts
A DC body that was rendered under cutover is compared post-rollback where normalize_outbound is back to identity, breaking the baseline/local match established during cutover
findings.suggested_fix: In disparaged-parodistic-shrew, extend the rollback AC (or add a new one) to drive a corpus body through: cutover ON -> push rendered wire -> flag OFF -> assert the next plain-wire pass emits zero body update and zero conflict for that already-rendered body, on both Cloud and DC; document that the DC rendered form is not reversible to the original Markdown, so 'rollback' means the reverted path must tolerate the residual rendered remote, not restore the pre-cutover bytes.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add acceptance criteria covering DC pandoc timeout enforcement, process-group termination, the dc_pandoc_timeout_s config-key wiring, and GPL/SBOM recording.
evidence: Deliverables: 'Bound subprocess work per field. Kill the process group on timeout... Add reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s to config schema, config docs, environment mapping, plus config golden. Record GPL/SBOM obligations'
No AC references timeout, process-group kill, GPL/SBOM, or dc_pandoc_timeout_s
findings.finding: The DC robustness story describes deliverables — bounded subprocess timeout, process-group kill on timeout, GPL/SBOM obligation recording, and the new reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s config key across schema/docs/env/golden — but no acceptance criterion covers timeout behavior, process-group termination, GPL/SBOM recording, or the config-key wiring.
findings.location: Child responsibilities → DC robustness; Acceptance Criteria
scenarios: The robustness story ships without a criterion proving the timeout kills the process group or that GPL/SBOM obligations were recorded.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the Problem/Design corpus figures with the CORPUS EVIDENCE CORRECTION (update or annotate the 99.65%/5,730/1,801 and structural-richness claims to the re-measured values) so the two sections do not contradict.
evidence: Problem: 'marklas reached 99.65% idempotent Markdown↔ADF round-trip over that corpus' and '1,801 tickets / 5,730 bodies'
Correction: 'the quoted figures are unreproducible... idempotence 99.75 percent; structural richness does NOT reproduce (22.8 vs 56.7 percent claimed); the 5,730-body cardinality is stale'
findings.finding: The Problem/Design narrative asserts the design is grounded in figures (99.65% idempotence, 1,801 tickets / 5,730 bodies, structural richness) that the later CORPUS EVIDENCE CORRECTION declares stale, unreproducible, and in the case of structural richness NON-reproducing (22.8% vs 56.7% claimed). Two sections make contradictory factual claims about the grounding corpus.
findings.location: Problem section vs 'CORPUS EVIDENCE CORRECTION' under Cloud ADF capability
scenarios: An executor reads the Problem section grounding and cites 99.65%/5,730 in design rationale, unaware the correction supersedes it.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the stale figures in Problem with the re-measured ones (99.75%, 4,996 bodies) and note that structural-richness enrichment did not reproduce, adjusting the design motivation accordingly.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add acceptance criteria that verify the Cloud no-marklas fallback and the DC no-pandoc/timeout identity fallback both preserve body content without loss.
evidence: 'imported lazily inside the three function bodies with ImportError routed to the plain adf.py fallback'
'Provide identity fallback when pandoc is absent' / 'Missing pandoc, timeout, or pathological input falls back without data loss'
findings.finding: The plan specifies two graceful-degradation paths as deliverables — the Cloud ImportError→plain adf.py fallback when the marklas optional extra is absent, and the DC identity fallback when pandoc is absent/times out — but no acceptance criterion verifies either fallback preserves content.
findings.location: Child responsibilities → Cloud ADF capability and DC renderer capability; Acceptance Criteria
scenarios: An environment without the marklas extra installed, or a DC host without the bundled pandoc, exercises the fallback path unverified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify a cross-platform subprocess-timeout kill for the DC renderer (POSIX process-group kill AND a Windows-compatible termination path, e.g. Popen.kill / job-object / creationflags), so the timeout fallback works on Windows CI and workstations.
evidence: Plan quote: 'Bound subprocess work per field. Kill the process group on timeout. Fall back without content loss.'
os.killpg and preexec_fn=os.setsid are unavailable on Windows; CreateProcess job objects / process-group flags differ.
Support matrix includes Windows developer workstations and Windows CI runners.
findings.finding: The DC robustness story specifies 'Kill the process group on timeout' as the subprocess-termination mechanism, but process-group kill (os.killpg / preexec_fn=os.setsid) is POSIX-specific and has no direct equivalent on Windows. The plan does not name a Windows-compatible termination path.
findings.location: Child responsibilities → DC robustness: 'Kill the process group on timeout.'
scenarios: Windows developer workstation or Windows CI runner: when pandoc exceeds dc_pandoc_timeout_s, the process-group kill call raises AttributeError/OSError (killpg absent) instead of terminating pandoc and falling back — the operator observes a crash or a hung/leaked pandoc process rather than the promised graceful identity fallback.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the two-asymmetric-codec + state-based echo-safety architecture and the marklas optional-extra dependency-contract decision in an ADR (or extend ADR-0026), not only in the plan body.
evidence: Plan: 'Use two asymmetric codecs behind one state-based echo-safety layer' — a new pattern.
Only ADR-0026 (baseline) is cited; the new codec architecture and the operator-approved deviation from the vendor plan live only in the plan body.
T5e sub-check: a novel architectural decision should be captured in an ADR / AGENTS.md / design-doc update.
findings.finding: The plan introduces a novel two-asymmetric-codec architecture behind a state-based echo-safety layer, but only references the pre-existing ADR-0026 (for the baseline mechanism). The new asymmetric-codec + echo-safety design decision and the marklas optional-extra deviation are captured inline in the plan rather than in an ADR/design-doc.
findings.location: Design section + DEVIATION note under Cloud ADF capability
scenarios: A future maintainer reading the repo (not this plan) encounters AdfCodec/WikiTextCodec asymmetry and the marklas optional-extra dependency-contract decision with no durable ADR explaining why one path is bidirectional and the other one-way, risking regression of the dependency-free-engine contract.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-state the Problem/Design grounding on the re-measured live-store basis (idempotence 99.75%, 4,996 unique bodies, structural richness 22.8%) instead of the retracted 99.65% / 1,801-ticket / 5,730-body figures, so the positive rationale for the pandoc dependency and marklas optional-extra is anchored to evidence the plan does not itself refute.
evidence: Problem: 'marklas reached 99.65% idempotent Markdown↔ADF round-trip over that corpus'
Problem: 'grounded in six experiments over the authoritative rebar export (1,801 tickets / 5,730 bodies)'

CORRECTION: 'the 2026-08-03 export/parity artifacts no longer exist, so the quoted figures are unreproducible ... structural richness does NOT reproduce (22.8 vs 56.7 percent claimed); the 5,730-body cardinality is stale'

The chosen mechanism is still defensible because thresholds are re-set from live measurement (99.75%); only the stated rationale is stale, so this is a rationale/evidence defect, not a mechanism defect.
findings.finding: The plan's fitness/soundness rationale is grounded in figures the plan itself retracts: the Problem and Design sections cite 99.65% idempotent round-trip over '1,801 tickets / 5,730 bodies' as the authoritative basis, but the CORPUS EVIDENCE CORRECTION states those artifacts 'no longer exist', the figures are 'unreproducible', structural richness 'does NOT reproduce (22.8 vs 56.7 percent claimed)', and the 5,730-body cardinality is 'stale'. The positive rationale for adopting a heavier solution (subprocess pandoc dependency, a new pinned optional extra, GPL/SBOM obligations) therefore rests on a premise the plan contradicts internally.
findings.location: Problem section ("99.65% idempotent", "1,801 tickets / 5,730 bodies", "session log 5eb0-52a3-45f0-43e5") vs Child responsibilities > Cloud ADF capability ("CORPUS EVIDENCE CORRECTION")
scenarios: An implementer or reviewer takes the Problem-section figures at face value and over- or under-scopes the effort relative to the true (re-measured) value of the feature.
The structural-richness delta (22.8% vs 56.7%) materially changes how much native rich text the cutover actually produces, affecting the cost/benefit of the pandoc + optional-extra complexity.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Problem and Design sections replace the retracted corpus figures with the re-measured ones from the CORPUS EVIDENCE CORRECTION, and fold the correction's caveats (structural richness lower than originally claimed) into the rationale for why the DC path is one-way/lossy and the Cloud path is the fully-bidirectional one.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Document why marklas was chosen over competing Markdown⇄ADF libraries (e.g. adflux's advertised lossless round-trip, marklassian-py, md-to-adf, atlas_doc_parser), including why the 99.75% measured idempotence is acceptable versus a library claiming losslessness.
evidence: Plan pins marklas and quotes idempotence 99.75% (i.e. NOT lossless) after the corpus correction.
Retrieved PyPI/GitHub: adflux (mikejhill/adflux) advertises 'Round-trips losslessly, including ADF-only constructs like panels, status badges, mentions, task lists, expand sections, and macros'.
Retrieved: marklassian-py (mbroton), md-to-adf (PyPI), atlas_doc_parser, pyadf (YoungseokCh) all provide Markdown/ADF conversion.
marklas PyPI confirms ADF-only features preserved as HTML elements with adf attributes — the same mechanism competitors claim.
findings.finding: The plan selects marklas as the Cloud Markdown⇄ADF backend without weighing it against several competing, actively-published Python libraries that offer the same capability — some claiming lossless round-trip — so the dependency choice is under-justified as prior art.
findings.location: Design § Cloud ADF capability; 'backed by marklas as a PINNED OPTIONAL EXTRA'
scenarios: Reviewer/operator asks why marklas over a library advertising lossless round-trip and native ADF-only construct fidelity, given marklas measured at 99.75%.
A marklas idempotence miss on a corpus body that a lossless alternative would have preserved.
